messages:
NOC-Bot: 🔔 Alert: Multiple egress failures detected from brazil-south2 (brs2). Increased 5xx to edge egress, some routes flapping. Auto-detection triggered P0 page. Logs attached to incident: link to logs (internal).
PagerDuty: Paging Alex P (oncall) — escalation policy applied.
Alex P (oncall): On it. I see spike in NAT gateway errors and a handful of BGP peer resets. Checking route tables and gateway health.
Diego S: Noted. Traffic to external peering is ~30% failing; internal probes show high TCP resets from the brs2 egress edge.
Maya R: Can we start failover to the secondary egress cluster in sa-east1? Runbook suggests controlled reroute if peer instability >10% for >5min.
Alex P (oncall): Agree. Starting controlled reroute to sa-east1. Will keep latency routing weight low to avoid big perf hit. Executing in 1m.
Carlos G: FYI support is prepping customer comms for affected customers in LatAm, will need ETA and scope.
Support L2: We are seeing a handful of elevated error reports from a customer in fintech-sandbox and two small SaaS customers. Triage links in thread.
Alex P (oncall): Action plan: 1) Apply emergency route diversion for brs2 -> sa-east1 for non-low-latency traffic. 2) Mark affected peering as degraded in routing layer. 3) Post status page and customer notice drafts. 4) Keep paging open until stable.
Diego S: Reroute step (control plane):
```
# internal routing API
curl -X POST "https://internal-api.redwood/services/routing/divert" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"region":"brazil-south2","target":"sa-east1","percent":30,"reason":"peer instability"}'
```
Doing incremental 30% now.
Alex P (oncall): 30% diverted. Monitoring metrics.
NOC-Bot: Update: egress errors from brs2 decreased by ~18% after 30% diversion. Peer resets trending down but still above baseline.
Maya R: Recommend ramp to 70% if errors don't drop further in 3 minutes.
Alex P (oncall): Ramping to 70% now.
Support L2: Customer impact summary for support queue: some generation requests return 502/504 during the window; affected requests mostly to external integrations (webhooks, external APIs). Internal model serving still healthy.
Product Comms: Drafting status page now. Proposed public status item:
```
Summary: We are investigating elevated external egress failures impacting customers in Brazil (brazil-south2). Some requests to external integrations may see increased errors or timeouts. We have initiated traffic diversion to sa-east1 to mitigate impact.
Current status: Mitigating — traffic diversion in progress
Region: brazil-south2
Affected services: external egress (outbound HTTP to peer networks)
Impact: Increased 5xx and timeouts for requests that call external third-party endpoints; core model inference remains available.
ETA: Investigating; will update within 30 minutes.
```
Product Comms: Also drafting targeted customer message for affected enterprise customers:
```
Subject: Incident: External egress instability affecting Brazil region
Hi — we're investigating an issue affecting outbound network requests from our brazil-south2 region. You may see intermittent 502/504 errors for requests that contact external endpoints. We've routed traffic to an alternate egress region (sa-east1) to reduce impact and are monitoring. No action is required on your side. We'll follow up with a full incident postmortem.
```
Legal: Keep me looped for any regulatory customers — Brazil-related data residency customers need an extra note if traffic leaves the region. Do not send the customer message to regulated customers without approval.
Product Comms: Good catch. We'll prepare two variants: one for regulated/regional-data-residency customers and one generic.
Alex P (oncall): Diversion at 70% completed. Errors dropped another ~35%. Latency increase for diverted paths ~45ms median, acceptable.
NOC-Bot: Monitoring alert: downstream peering stabilization trending positive. If stable for 10m, recommend slow rollback of diversion.
Diego S: Root cause hypothesis: transient peering flap with our third-party transit provider causing TCP resets. We'll request peering vendor logs.
Carlos G: Support: drafting targeted customer list now. Will hold regulated customers' emails until Legal signs off.
Support L2: ETA for customer-first update: 15-20 minutes once Product Comms finalizes copy.
Alex P (oncall): Next actions: 1) Keep page updated (Product Comms). 2) Keep paging open and monitor for 10m stable. 3) If stable, start 10% decrements every 2m to move traffic back.
Product Comms: Posting status page now (internal draft posted for review). Command to push status (internal tool):
```
# push to status page (internal)
POST /v1/status/incidents
{ "region": "brazil-south2", "status": "mitigating", "short_summary": "External egress failures — traffic diversion in progress", "update": "We have diverted a majority of traffic to sa-east1 while we work with our peering provider." }
```
Product Comms: Internal comms template for ops channels:
"""
BRIEF: brs2 external egress instability. Mitigating by diverting traffic to sa-east1. Impact: outbound calls to third-party APIs may see 502/504; model inference unaffected.
ACTIONS: Diversion applied; monitoring; vendor engagement ongoing; customer comms queued (regulated customers require Legal approval).
NEXT UPDATE: Will update in 15 minutes or on significant change.
"""
Support L2: Sent internal queue note to affected customers (non-regulated). Copy of message attached in ticket.
Legal: Approved non-regulated message. Regulated variant pending 1:1 with ops lead.
Alex P (oncall): 10m stable reached, starting gradual rollback: -10% every 2m.
NOC-Bot: Note: Keep oncall paging channel open until rollback completes and peering vendor confirms stable.
Carlos G: Postmortem owners? Suggest Diego + Alex + Maya for ops; Carlos for customer comms; Product Comms for timeline.
Product Comms: Logged owners. Will prepare customer follow-up and community post once root cause confirmed.
Diego S: Request to peering vendor submitted. Ticket ID: PV-12345.
Alex P (oncall): Rollback complete. Metrics normalizing. Closing page in 30m if no regressions.
Support L2: Closing impacted support tickets as stabilization confirmed; will reopen if customers report further issues.
Product Comms: Final status page update draft:
"""
Resolved: We mitigated an outage affecting external egress from brazil-south2 by diverting traffic while we worked with our peering provider to stabilize the connection. Impacted customers may have seen intermittent 502/504 on calls to external endpoints. Core model inference availability was not impacted. A detailed postmortem will be published in the next 72 hours.
"""
Legal: Please include the note about any traffic temporarily leaving region for non-regulated customers. For regulated ones, we need an explicit approval and a copy of the vendor timeline before sending.
Alex P (oncall): Thanks everyone. Handing to postmortem owners. Closing the page now and will file incident for RCA.
NOC-Bot: Incident resolved — monitoring continues."
